newsitem.title: USA: Highlights of New York State Assembly school plan.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of New York State Assembly school plan.

text.p: The New York State Assembly on Wednesday proposed a five-year, $5.5 billion education plan that will compete in some areas with legislation put forward by the Senate and Gov. George Pataki.

The Assembly's plan includes a $2 billion school bond, and would raise to 50 percent how much Albany reimbursed localities for bonds they issued for capital construction. This would let the state finance a total of $6 billion for such programs.
Highlights of the Assembly's new plan follow.
--$60 million would be earmarked each year by 2002 to pay for full-day kindergarten for the 65,000 students for whom it now is not offered.
--$445 million would be provided to cover the full cost of cutting the size of classes from kindergarten through third-grade to no more than 20 pupils.
--Albany would fund $1 billion by 2002 or nearly 90 percent of pre-kindergarten for every four-year old.
--An increase of $228 million would be spent on textbooks and $83 million on technology aids for every school in the state.
--About $50 million would be spent for new teacher training initiatives.
